provenance.title: Long File
provenance.method: git archive <commit> | tar -x -C <dir> && node cmd/cheasee-pi/embedded/docker/codeflow/run-analysis.mjs <dir> <codeflow-ui> <out>; metric read from report.json -> patterns["Long File"].metrics.files
provenance.metric: patterns[name === "Long File"].files — analyzed files where isCode !== false && lines && lines > 500 (index.html:1411-1412, pinned ref below). `lines = content.split("\n").length`, so a trailing newline counts: 500 newline-segments is not flagged, 501 is. `isCode` gates files whose extension is absent from codeExts/scriptContainerExts — notably `.mts`, `.json` and `.md` — so this record, its fixture and its oracle can never be reduction sources.
provenance.baseCountNote: the issue was filed with 61 files at analyzedAt 1791738325602 against the then-main. The immutable base below (origin/main after #2001/#2002/#2003/#2004) reports 35 flagged files: the earlier refactors already split part of the filed set. Acceptance is the drop on the delivered branch, not the filed number.
provenance.filesNote: `files` is the snapshot's tracked-file count (`git ls-tree -r --name-only <commit> | wc -l`), a reproducible proxy for the analyzer's parsed-file count. Only its ordering matters here: `after.files > before.files` proves the drop did not come from deleting files.
provenance.afterTipNote: the after snapshot is commit 39e62d9e, the last commit of this branch that changes scored code; later commits touch only register artifacts (`.json`/`.mts`/`.md`, never scored) and EOF whitespace strips, so the Long File count and the flagged set are identical on every post-split commit. `7bcbeefd` differs from 39e62d9e only by this fixture, the mirror, the oracle block, the reference doc and the strips in nine split files. `after.files`/`after.codeFiles` are 39e62d9e's tracked/scored counts. The `long file metric oracle (issue #2005)` block in `test/codeflow-run-analysis.test.mts` recomputes the predicate over the delivered tree with the mirror in `test/fixtures/long-file-mirror.mts`, so this envelope cannot drift from the source it describes. One later commit does change scored code: the #2026 dead-code reference rule merged onto this branch and took `cmd/cheasee-pi/embedded/docker/codeflow/fp-filter.js` past 500 segments, so `after.longFileCount` is the delivered tree's 17 and that file joins the deferrals below — the register is maintained, not frozen.

tradeoffs.longFile: 35 -> 16 flagged files (-19, -54.3 %). The 19 split families each leave the flagged set because every original and every sibling lands <= 500 raw segments (pinned by test/long-file-refactor-2005.test.mts). The residual 16 are the deferrals below: 15 Rust files under embedded/docker/ui and codeflow/server.py. Later, the #2026 dead-code reference rule merged onto this branch and took codeflow/fp-filter.js past 500 segments, so `after.longFileCount` is re-anchored to the delivered tree's 17 and the file is recorded as a third deferral (same boundary reason as server.py).
tradeoffs.coupling: splitting mints files that reference the same package-level helpers as their siblings, so the #2002 coupling heuristic (a file that references more than 8 defining files) can count a new sibling as coupled. Recorded, not hidden: the change is scoped to Long File.
tradeoffs.complexity: the split moves whole declarations verbatim, but each new sibling carries its own raw-text branch tokens (comments and string literals included) under the `1 + Σ(hits) > 30` ceiling. A handful of new siblings can edge over it; recorded for the same reason.
tradeoffs.approach: behaviour-preserving relocation only. Production originals keep their exported names as explicit named re-exports (no `export *`); test `describe` blocks and Go `func Test…` declarations move verbatim, so the existing suites are the verification; the Python safety-net suite keeps `python3 test/dependency-existence-check.test.py` as its entry.

deferred.reason: no Rust toolchain in the pipeline image — splits under embedded/docker/ui cannot be compiled or tested in-gate (#2002/#2003/#2004 precedent); the non-Rust drop already satisfies the acceptance criterion

the embedded server carries inline _BRIDGE_JS/_UI_REWRITES assets whose module boundaries are the Dockerfile COPY set; splitting it changes the copy-set boundary in the same commit, so it is deferred to the change that owns that guard

single-file served asset: the Dockerfile COPY set and the one `<script src="fp-filter.js">` tag pinned by the Go and bridge suites are its module boundary, so splitting it changes that contract in the same commit. It crossed 500 segments when the #2026 dead-code reference rule landed; deferred to the change that owns the boundary guard
